context: Add a canonical registry create command and make every other command open-only. Preflight an existing database read-only, validate immutable identity and role, derive repository authority from the recorded owner rather than cwd, and only then reopen for writes or approved migrations. Decision gate: stop if a valid primary checkout cannot be identified unambiguously, if backward compatibility would silently select a local worktree database, or if any proposal introduces multiple operational writers.
description: Make the primary checkout's .bossmode/control.db the sole operational task, run, evaluation, and resource authority. Split explicit database creation from opening, bind immutable registry identity to the Git common directory and primary checkout, and prevent linked worktrees or scheduler jobs from creating or migrating operational state. Temporary certification databases remain explicitly ephemeral and cannot be adopted into operational history.

anti_patterns.dont: Introduce init, rebind, or other aliases
anti_patterns.instead: Use one canonical spelling and test it
anti_patterns.why: Bossmode naming policy forbids additive aliases and repurposed tokens

anti_patterns.dont: Keep per-worktree operational registries and merge or copy them later
anti_patterns.instead: Write all operational bookkeeping through the central supervisor
anti_patterns.why: .bossmode is ignored and histories have no safe collision protocol

anti_patterns.instead: Use the immutable validated registry owner and Git common directory
anti_patterns.why: The caller may be a linked worktree or unrelated directory

preserves.behavior: Ephemeral test and certification databases can never become operational through path selection or import.
Every CLI spelling remains canonical, documented, and directly invoked by a test.
Registry ownership is checked before any filesystem or SQLite mutation.
There is exactly one operational registry per repository and it is owned by the primary checkout.
